extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, and Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually collected in three stages: the authors selected 30 subjects from six disciplines, recruited over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and create new questions where necessary, and assembled a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources, later excluding about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of the collected problems were excluded from the benchmark because they were classified as very easy and did not align with the benchmark design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks; collected from online sources, textbooks, lecture materials, free online resources, quizzes, and other study materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoid sources prohibiting copy and redistribution, select questions without immediately available answers, ensure all questions contain one or more images, are written in English, meet college-level difficulty, are unambiguous, and annotate fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation if available; suspected duplicates were identified via lexical overlap and source URL similarity and reviewed by authors, problems were checked for format and typos, and authors categorized difficulty levels and excluded about 10% classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: JSON file format; user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to eliminate duplications; a secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence; regular audits of random samples were conducted; ambiguities were flagged for detailed review and collaboratively examined in team meetings; authors also checked format and typos, categorized problems into four difficulty levels, and excluded approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: over 50 university students specializing in these majors; 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: lexical overlap and source URL similarity
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Level 3, or Expert AGI, marks a critical milestone. It denotes an AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI

extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found.
